svg.title: Fig. 181(a) — An isolated point at the origin: x²(y² − 1) = y⁴
svg.desc: Redrawn from Robert C. Yates, A Handbook on Curves and Their Properties (1947), Fig. 181(a), page 200. Section: sketching.

g.data-text: The box with its axes, and the equation x²(y² − 1) = y⁴.
The asymptotes: dividing by y² the curve is x² = y⁴/(y² − 1), so x → ∞ as y → ±1 (the horizontal asymptotes y = ±1) and x ≈ ±y for large y (the diagonals y = ±x). Draw the four lines.
Draw the four branches x = ±y²/√(y² − 1) for |y| > 1: each comes in along a horizontal asymptote, turns and leaves along a diagonal one.
The origin satisfies the equation but no real branch passes through it: it is an isolated point (the lowest-degree term x² = 0 would suggest a cusp, but y⁴ is too small to make one).
